subject: Enterprise ops-leveling: availability packages & incident coverage
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmecloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-08-29T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Inquiry: uptime guarantees, credits & 24/7 escalation for enterprise plan

Hi Vanessa,

We ran your trial load against a few internal services and like the performance. Before we proceed to a POC we'll need clarity on a couple of items related to availability and support for a production rollout:

- Uptime tiers you offer (SLO targets) and how they map to credits
- Response targets for Sev1/Sev2 incidents (initial ack, mitigation SLA, full resolution expectations)
- 24/7 escalation coverage and direct contact (on-call or TAM) options
- Pricing for the above (monthly and any volume/commit discounts) and whether reserved capacity is required to get uptime SLAs

Can you send a simple pricing matrix and a sample credit table? Procurement is particularly interested in how credits are calculated and any carve-outs. Also please confirm SOC 2 availability and whether audit logs can be retained for 24 months.

If useful we can schedule a 30-min call this week. Thanks — Emily

--
Emily Zhang
Head of Cloud Platform, Acme Cloud
emily.zhang@acmecloud.com

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmecloud.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-29T13:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: uptime guarantees, credits & 24/7 escalation for enterprise plan

Thanks Emily — great to hear the trial looked good. I'm copying Marissa (commercial lead) to keep her in the loop.

Short answers up front, then a quick propose-and-schedule:

Options (ballpark SLOs & coverage):
- Standard: 99.9% uptime, business-hours support (M–F), next-business-day rolling response for Sev2, no guaranteed 24/7 on-call.
- Premium: 99.95% uptime, 24/7 incident intake, 1-hour initial response for Sev1, dedicated escalation contact (email + phone), recommended for production customer-facing workloads.
- Enterprise Plus: 99.99% uptime target, 15-minute initial objective for Sev1, dedicated TAM + named on-call escalation, custom routing and optional reserved capacity.

Pricing (ballpark, monthly):
- Standard: base usage pricing + $0/month support fee
- Premium: +$7k/month
- Enterprise Plus: +$25k/month (includes 24/7 ops and named escalation)

Discounts: we offer volume/commit discounts on reserved capacity (examples: 12-month commit = typically 15% off; 24-month commit = up to 20% depending on capacity size and scope).

Credits: We do provide service credits for SLA misses; the precise table is contractual and legal needs to sign off (we can share a sample credit table).

Attachments: I've attached a one-page starter proposal (proposal_redwood_enterprise_v1.pdf) that maps features to price tiers and an overview of onboarding options.

Next steps: can you do Wed 9/2 10am PT or Thu 9/3 2pm PT for a 30-min call? We can walk through the credit table and your retention/audit requirements.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmecloud.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmecloud.com
Date: 2026-08-30T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: uptime guarantees, credits & 24/7 escalation for enterprise plan

Thanks Vanessa — Wed 9/2 10am PT works.

A couple of clarifying asks to prep the meeting: can you confirm whether the 99.99% Enterprise Plus option requires reserved capacity (and if so, what minimum footprint)? Also we need the explicit credit table up front (we've had procurement go back and forth on ambiguous credit language in prior deals).

On discounts: we're evaluating a 12–24 month commit. If you can show a discounted price that includes an initial TAM + a 2-week onboarding SOW (or a credit towards it), that will make the commercial review much easier.

Finally — what are the legal carve-outs for maintenance windows and force majeure? Procurement will flag any hard no on hidden carve-outs.

— Emily

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Inquiry: uptime guarantees, credits & 24/7 escalation for enterprise plan

Marissa / Rishi — forwarding Acme's asks. They're a mid-sized public cloud provider evaluating a production rollout. Key commercial asks: explicit credit table, 99.99 option, TAM + 2-week onboarding included or credited, and a meaningful commit discount.

My propose: offer 20% off Enterprise Plus pricing for a 12-month reserved capacity commit of at least 8 reserved units (we've benchmarked this as their likely footprint). Include a one-time onboarding credit of $25,000 and provide TAM support for the first 3 months (then convert to paid TAM at standard rate). Legal will need to take the SLA credit language, but we can share a sample.

If 20% needs escalation, recommend we hold at 15% and ask for finance sign-off for the extra 5%. Thoughts? Also any restriction on promising the 15-minute objective for Sev1 in writing?

Thanks — Vanessa

--
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Inquiry: uptime guarantees, credits & 24/7 escalation for enterprise plan

Vanessa — good summary. I agree with offering 20% off Enterprise Plus if they sign a 12-month reserved capacity (min 8 units) and accept the standard reserved-capacity billing terms. Approve the one-time $25k onboarding credit.

On the Sev1 objective: don't promise an absolute "15-minute resolution" — position it as an initial response objective/acknowledgement window with acceleration to mitigation pathways and a named escalation loop. That's defensible in the SLA and legal won't object.

I'll prepare a redline of the sample credit table and attach it to our reply for transparency (see internal attachment: Acme_SLA_ask_redline.pdf). We should also nudge Legal to prepare an explicit credit calculation example for procurement.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acmecloud.com>, procurement@acmecloud.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-31T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry: uptime guarantees, credits & 24/7 escalation for enterprise plan

Emily — thanks for the call this morning. Attached are the updated materials we discussed: a redlined sample credit table and an updated proposal that reflects the negotiated commercial terms.

Summary of the commercial offer (Enterprise Plus):
- SLO objective: 99.99% (contract will include objective language and defined measurement windows)
- Incident intake: 24/7 with named escalation contact + TAM assigned for implementation and first 3 months
- Initial response objective for Sev1: 15 minutes to acknowledge and begin escalation (contract language will frame this as an objective and include mitigation pathways and named contacts)
- Price: Enterprise Plus base $25k/month; with 12-month reserved capacity commit (min 8 units) we will apply a 20% discount -> $20k/month equivalent support fee.
- One-time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied to first invoice (covers first 2-week SOW).
- SLA credits: attached redline contains example credit calculations; legal to finalize final wording.

Attachments: Acme_SLA_ask_redline.pdf, proposal_redwood_enterprise_v1.pdf

Next steps:
1) I'll upload the commercial draft to DocuSign once legal finalizes the credit language (link will be shared).
2) If procurement is happy with the sample credit table, we can convert to an LOI and reserve the capacity.

Let me know if you want me to loop in Legal or Solutions for a short session on the credit calculation.

Best,

Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
